mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last week signals more commuting and downtown circulation, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as weekday trips convert into shopping and dining visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days after a one-week increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remains depressed, discretionary trips shift toward local errands and nearby shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC above its recent average within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -15 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls or stays below its last-four-week mean over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above +15 and WORKPLACES staying below -15.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent drop in TRANSIT indicates weaker access to high-street retail by public transport, which should reduce RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks if the transit decline is not offset by a matching rise in workplace attendance.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -33 and stays there for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the prior 28 days within four weeks after TRANSIT remains below -33 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in PARKS use captures favorable weather and outdoor leisure substitution, which pulls spending away from indoor retail and pushes RETAIL_REC down within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week after PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC remains depressed, the same local-trip demand pattern spills over into adjacent retail visits, producing a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above +4 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM stays above +4 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES implies stronger city-center activity, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as shopping is combined with commuting and lunch-time trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its previous 28-day mean over the next 28 days when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward.

mechanism_narrative: If the gap between RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES widens further, commuting frictions and caution reduce discretionary high-street visits, making RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds WORKPLACES by at least 35 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-four-week average within 14 days when RESIDENTIAL is at least 35 points above WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS alongside a flatter RESIDENTIAL series signals broader mobility normalization that supports shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 28 days over the next four weeks when PARKS improves and RESIDENTIAL stays near its recent level.
